Usage: cw <command> [options]

Authoring the charter:
  cw init                 Set this repository up under a charter
  cw build                Compile the charter into the files each agent reads
  cw list                 Say what the charter holds
  cw kinds [kind]         Say which kinds a charter is written in, and what one
                          of them requires
  cw add <kind> <id>      Write a new primitive of one kind, holding what that
                          kind requires
  cw edit <id>            Open the file of one primitive in your editor
  cw remove <id>          Delete the file of one primitive this repository
                          authored
  cw explain <id>         Say which file declares an id, and which layer it came
                          from
  cw doctor               Check this repository: agents, charter, vendors, and
                          what is built
  cw context              Say how many tokens the charter puts into the agent's
                          main context
  cw sessions             Sum up the tokens of the sessions kept on this
                          machine, by day and by session
  cw test                 Resolve every situation under
                          .cw/charter/<charter>/test/ against the charter
  cw eval                 Put every case under .cw/charter/<charter>/eval/ to
                          the real agent under promptfoo
  cw eval-analyze         Read evaluation results, tool evidence and agent
                          session paths without running an agent
  cw suite                add, edit, remove
  cw vendor               init, add, inject, remove, list
  cw mcp                  auth

Running it:
  cw run mcp              Serve every mcp origin the charter reaches to your
                          agent, over stdio
  cw run sensor <signal>  Run every sensor of a signal, as the agent's one hook
                          for it
  cw run portal           Serve this repository's charter to a browser on this
                          machine

Options:
      --version  Show version number                                   [boolean]
  -h, --help     Show help                                             [boolean]
<version>

Author your first rule with "cw add guide <id> --charter=<charter>", or ask your agent to write one, then run "cw build".

Kinds
  guide     a touched file matches one of its `globs`, or every turn where globs
            are not specified
  sensor    the `signal` it names is raised, and the harness runs what it says
            to `run`
  skill     one of its `triggers` matches what is being asked
  playbook  one of its `triggers` matches; the body is a sequence of skills
  agent     it is spawned by id, holding the `tools` it lists and nothing else —
            an mcp origin as `[[<id>]]`, or one of its tools as
            `[[<id>]]:<tool>`
  posture   always, wherever the agent can be told what to `allow` and what to
            `deny`
  corpus    a primitive's `rationale` cites it — the reasoning, read when
            someone asks why
  mixin     never on its own: its body is lent to the primitives that pull it in
  mcp       a primitive's body names it as `[[<id>]]` — an mcp origin outside
            the repository, reached through `cw run mcp`
  script    a primitive names it as `[[<id>]]`, or a sensor runs it — its
            assets, copied to `$CW_OUT/script/<id>/`, of which its
            `executionPath` names the one to run
  template  a primitive names it as `[[<id>]]` — a file the agent fills or
            copies, written as its body

# Cherry Works

This folder holds the charter that governs the coding agents working in this repository, kept by [Cherry Works](https://github.com/tamnguyenvt/cherry-works). It was set up with `cw` <version>.

- `charter/` — the charter: `primitive/` for what this repository authors, one folder per kind; `test/` and `eval/` for its tests and eval cases; `vendor/` for charters and skills installed with `cw vendor add`, read-only.
- `out/` — what `cw build` compiles the charter to; never edit it.
- `settings.json` — what this repository was set up with.

## Author it

- Ask your agent to run the `/cw-author` skill: it asks what a primitive needs and writes it.
- Or run `cw run portal` and author it in the browser.

Then run `cw build` to lay the charter out for every agent.

# Charter

This repository is governed by a charter — the standards it authored under `.cw/charter/`, which constrain whatever coding agent runs here. Every surface an agent reads, this file included, is generated from that charter: do not edit them, edit the primitive behind them.

## Read first

Read [catalogue.json](./catalogue.json) for shared primitives and `catalogue.<provider>.json` linked from your agent's entry file for primitives restricted to your provider. Entries are not repeated between these files. Each entry lists kind, id, description, file and globs. Use these two catalogues and open a file when its activation condition below is met.

## When each kind applies

- **guide** — a touched file matches one of its `globs`, or every turn where globs are not specified.
- **sensor** — the `signal` it names is raised, and the harness runs what it says to `run`.
- **skill** — one of its `triggers` matches what is being asked.
- **playbook** — one of its `triggers` matches; the body is a sequence of skills.
- **agent** — it is spawned by id, holding the `tools` it lists and nothing else — an mcp origin as `[[<id>]]`, or one of its tools as `[[<id>]]:<tool>`.
- **posture** — always, wherever the agent can be told what to `allow` and what to `deny`.
- **corpus** — a primitive's `rationale` cites it — the reasoning, read when someone asks why.
- **mixin** — never on its own: its body is lent to the primitives that pull it in.
- **mcp** — a primitive's body names it as `[[<id>]]` — an mcp origin outside the repository, reached through `cw run mcp`.
- **script** — a primitive names it as `[[<id>]]`, or a sensor runs it — its assets, copied to `./script/<id>/`, of which its `executionPath` names the one to run.
- **template** — a primitive names it as `[[<id>]]` — a file the agent fills or copies, written as its body.

## One id, one primitive

An id names one primitive in the whole charter, whatever its kind: it is all a primitive is named by — bare in a header, a test or a command, and as `[[<id>]]` in a body, a sensor's `run` or an agent's `tools` — whether this repository authored it, installed it from a vendor, or the engine brought it. Nothing overrides anything — two files claiming one id is an error the charter refuses to build with.

This script is cw's own. It comes with the engine, is not authored in this
repository, and cannot be changed here.

Run when the agent stops, with Claude Code's Stop event on its standard input,
it counts the session's tokens so far — input, output, written to and read from
the cache — subagents included, off Claude Code's own transcript of the
session. Each stop is kept as one line of
`<session id>/session-analysis.jsonl`, on this machine: under
`~/.cherry-works/<the repository's path>/`, each character of the path that is
not a letter or a digit written as a dash, or in the `sessionAnalysisFolder`
of `.cw/settings.json`. Nothing is committed or sent
anywhere.

When the session crosses a mark — every 100,000 tokens, or the
`sessionContextMark` of `.cw/settings.json` — the developer is shown one line with
its tokens. The model is sent nothing of it.

A transcript it cannot read is left alone: nothing is shown or kept, and the
agent stops as it would have.
